title: Reproducible complete Companion integration evidence
scope: A self-contained canonical integration lab that lets any maintainer independently exercise the real Bitfocus Companion application and the real OverlayKit OSS server across a non-loopback Ubuntu 24.04 LTS network boundary.
summary: A maintainer starts two clean Linux nodes from public inputs, provisions ephemeral local device authority, loads the exact OverlayKit module into the actual Companion application, invokes Show-scoped visibility commands, and obtains causally bound visual and machine-readable evidence for every supported feedback state and timing claim.

actors.label: OverlayKit maintainer
actors.description: Reproduces and reviews the complete integration evidence without private infrastructure or undocumented knowledge.

actors.label: Linux operator
actors.description: Invokes virtual Companion buttons and observes their projected production state.

actors.label: Bitfocus Companion application
actors.description: Loads the OverlayKit module, invokes actions, and renders feedback states in its real user interface.

actors.label: OverlayKit OSS server
actors.description: Owns local device admission, command outcomes, and authoritative production state.

terms.name: Canonical Integration Lab
terms.definition: A clean, reproducible two-node Ubuntu 24.04 LTS environment whose Companion and OverlayKit traffic crosses a non-loopback network boundary.

terms.name: Causal Evidence Receipt
terms.definition: A machine-readable record from one run that binds expected and observed UI state to the server event that justified it, the accepted evidence hash, timestamps, run identity, and exact component versions.

terms.name: Authoritative UI Projection
terms.definition: A Companion-visible state derived from accepted OverlayKit server evidence rather than optimistic UI, transport acknowledgement, or command result alone.

terms.name: Supplemental Lab Validation
terms.definition: Additional evidence from a real host or private network that may corroborate but never replace the canonical publicly reproducible lab.

requirements.statement: The canonical lab proves the complete Companion-to-OverlayKit application path rather than substituting the module host harness for either real product.
requirements.verification: Process identity, runtime version, loaded-module, endpoint, and traffic receipts from the same lab run.

requirements.statement: The lab uses the actual Bitfocus Companion application, the actual OverlayKit OSS server, and the exact governed module package with immutable build or artifact identities.
requirements.verification: Pinned Companion build or image digest, runtime-reported version, OverlayKit commit, module archive digest, and process inspection.

requirements.statement: Canonical evidence runs on two isolated Ubuntu 24.04 LTS nodes and crosses a non-loopback network boundary without depending on Tailscale.
requirements.verification: Node OS receipts, interface and route capture, non-loopback endpoint assertion, and packet or connection evidence.

requirements.statement: The real Companion UI visibly projects active, inactive, unknown, disconnected, failed, and unavailable, with every capture bound to a causal evidence receipt from the same run.
requirements.verification: Six UI captures plus validated receipts containing expected and observed state, server event, accepted evidence hash, timestamps, run identity, and exact versions.

requirements.statement: After a virtual button invocation, authoritative server state must be visible in Companion within three seconds; acknowledgement or result alone does not stop the timer, expiry projects unknown and fails that measurement, and later evidence cannot retroactively pass it.
requirements.verification: Monotonic invocation, server-evidence, and UI-observation timestamps with deterministic timeout and delayed-evidence cases.

requirements.statement: The canonical lab is self-contained and starts from public inputs with ephemeral local credentials and trust; it requires no cloud account, private service, private network identity, or maintainer-specific secret.
requirements.verification: Clean-room setup review, generated credential receipts, secret scan, and successful reproduction without external authentication.

userStories.need: independently reproduce the complete Bitfocus Companion-to-OverlayKit integration over a non-loopback LAN
userStories.outcome: the project can distinguish demonstrated application behavior from adapter assumptions without relying on a production workstation or private infrastructure
preconditions: The maintainer has a clean Linux machine capable of running two isolated Ubuntu 24.04 LTS nodes.
The repository and every required input are publicly obtainable.
The two nodes can communicate over a non-loopback local network.

acceptanceCriteria.given: two clean Ubuntu 24.04 LTS nodes and only public repository inputs
acceptanceCriteria.when: the maintainer starts the canonical lab
acceptanceCriteria.then: the actual OverlayKit server and actual Companion application become ready over a non-loopback network using locally provisioned ephemeral authority
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Automated setup plus OS, process, version, endpoint, trust, and readiness receipts.

acceptanceCriteria.given: the real Companion application has loaded the exact governed OverlayKit module and reached device.ready
acceptanceCriteria.when: the operator invokes show, hide, and toggle from virtual buttons
acceptanceCriteria.then: the real OverlayKit server applies each command and Companion changes state only from accepted authoritative evidence
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Command, server-state, signed-evidence, and Companion UI receipts for all three actions.

acceptanceCriteria.given: the lab can inject controlled state, disconnect, authority, and protocol conditions
acceptanceCriteria.when: each supported feedback condition is exercised
acceptanceCriteria.then: the actual Companion UI visibly shows active, inactive, unknown, disconnected, failed, and unavailable with one causal receipt per capture
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Six visual captures whose receipt hashes and run identity validate against the machine-readable evidence bundle.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a virtual visibility action is invoked
acceptanceCriteria.when: authoritative server state is or is not projected before the three-second deadline
acceptanceCriteria.then: the measurement passes only for timely authoritative projection; otherwise Companion shows unknown and the failed measurement remains failed after any late evidence
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Monotonic timing receipts for timely, acknowledgement-only, result-only, timeout, and late-evidence cases.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a maintainer begins from a clean supported machine with no Rodrigo-specific identity or private network access
acceptanceCriteria.when: the documented reproduction is followed from zero
acceptanceCriteria.then: the same assertions and evidence schema can be regenerated, while any llama or Tailscale run remains separately labeled supplemental
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Second clean-room execution and comparison of semantic assertions rather than environment-specific hashes.

workflows.title: Reproduce complete Companion integration evidence
steps: The maintainer obtains the repository and pinned public inputs on a clean Linux machine.
The lab creates two isolated Ubuntu 24.04 LTS nodes on a non-loopback local network.
The OverlayKit node generates ephemeral local device authority and starts the actual OSS server.
The Companion node starts the pinned actual application and loads the exact governed module package through the documented local-module path.
The module completes signed bootstrap, acknowledgement, and readiness against the OverlayKit node.
The operator invokes show, hide, and toggle from Companion virtual buttons.
The lab exercises normal, delayed, disconnected, failed, and unavailable conditions.
The evidence collector binds each visible UI state to the exact server event, evidence hash, time, run, and versions.
The verifier rejects missing, stale, mismatched, loopback-only, late, private-input, or semantically incomplete evidence.
An optional llama or Tailscale run is recorded separately as supplemental corroboration.

outOfScope: USB access, Stream Deck discovery, and physical key presses
Physical device button pixels and operator perception
npm publication and Bitfocus module registry admission
Linux distributions other than Ubuntu 24.04 LTS
Tailscale or the llama host as a canonical reproduction dependency
Support beyond the exact Companion, OverlayKit, module, Node, and container or VM identities exercised by the Slice
